privacy-policy: Last updated: 16 October 2026 About this policy The Pioneer Forest (TPF) is an independent, community-driven environmental initiative within the Pi Network ecosystem, operated by egal42. This policy applies to the TPF website, associated applications, direct Pi contributions, environmental records and Partner Pools. Privacy enquiries: egal42.pi@gmail.com . Information handled Depending on the activity, TPF may handle authenticated Pi usernames; payment IDs, transaction IDs, wallet addresses, amounts, memos and statuses; contribution and allocation records; voluntary messages; and limited security and technical information. Pi sign-in does not ordinarily provide TPF with Pi KYC identity documents. TPF never requests wallet passphrases or private keys. Purposes and legal bases Information is used to operate services, authenticate users, verify transactions, maintain environmental and participation records, answer enquiries, prevent abuse and comply with applicable obligations. Depending on the processing, the legal basis may be performance of an agreement (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)), legitimate interests in secure and reliable operation (Art. 6(1)(f)), legal obligations (Art. 6(1)(c)), or consent for optional uses (Art. 6(1)(a)). In-app payments and direct transfers For payments made through the TPF Pi app, payment records can be associated with the authenticated Pi username. The Developer Portal app currently uses Pi Testnet; separate direct wallet contributions already occur on Mainnet. A direct blockchain transfer does not itself establish a verified Pi username. TPF does not automatically publish a username together with a wallet address. Transparency and public records TPF publishes environmental records and verification links, which may include transaction references, certificates and voluntarily provided attribution. Blockchain transactions are publicly visible independently of TPF. Public blockchain records cannot normally be erased by TPF. Public attribution or account-to-wallet disclosure beyond what is necessary for the service should be optional and clearly explained. Service providers and transfers Relevant third parties may include Pi Network, website and application hosting providers, blockchain infrastructure and environmental providers such as Tree-Nation. Their own terms and privacy practices may apply. Processing outside the European Economic Area may occur; applicable transfer safeguards must be assessed for the actual providers used. Storage and retention TPF aims to minimize production logs and retain information only for as long as necessary for its purpose, including applicable transaction and recordkeeping obligations. Temporary technical logs should be kept shorter than records required for payment verification or legal compliance. Browser storage may be used for session information and local activity history. Consent will be requested for non-essential cookies or similar technologies where required. Your rights Where the GDPR applies, you may request access, correction, deletion, restriction or portability of personal data, object to certain processing, and withdraw consent where processing relies on consent. Rights may be limited by applicable law and immutable blockchain records. You may complain to a competent data protection authority. Contact egal42.pi@gmail.com . Updates This policy may be updated as TPF services develop. The latest version will appear on this page.
terms-of-service: Last updated: 16 October 2026 About TPF The Pioneer Forest (TPF) is an independent, community-driven environmental initiative within the Pi Network ecosystem, operated by egal42. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Pi Core Team. Contact: egal42.pi@gmail.com . Participation and Pi Network TPF services are primarily intended for Pi Network participants. Some functions require Pi authentication or a Pi Wallet. Pi Network manages its own account verification and KYC procedures; ordinary Pi authentication does not provide TPF with identity documents or necessarily confirm a user’s KYC status. Participants must comply with applicable law and platform rules. Wallet security TPF never asks for your Pi Wallet passphrase or private keys. Only enter your passphrase in the official Pi Wallet accessed through Pi Browser. Do not share it with anyone claiming to represent TPF. Contributions and payments TPF already accepts direct Mainnet Pi wallet contributions. Its Developer Portal app currently uses Testnet for payment testing; Testnet Pi is not a real Mainnet contribution. If Mainnet in-app payments are introduced, the applicable purpose and amount should be shown before confirmation. Blockchain transfers may be irreversible at network level, but this does not remove applicable legal remedies or consumer rights. Environmental activity and transparency TPF supports tree planting, reforestation and related environmental projects through independent providers. Project availability, methodology and outcomes vary. Unless an offer expressly says otherwise, participation does not grant ownership of trees, land, carbon credits, financial returns or governance rights. See Transparency & Scope for the project’s public reporting approach. Partner Pools Partner Pools have specific environmental backing and allocation rules set out in the relevant pool information. Partners may allocate benefits to eligible participants according to those rules. Public pool records may describe backing, allocations and remaining balances. Digital products and other offers Where TPF offers a digital product or other paid item, the specific offer describes what is supplied, the price and relevant conditions. A purchase is distinct from a voluntary contribution. Applicable mandatory consumer information, cancellation rights and other statutory protections remain in effect. Errors, refunds and support For failed, duplicate or incorrect transactions, contact egal42.pi@gmail.com with the relevant payment or transaction reference. Corrections, refunds and other remedies are handled according to the circumstances and applicable law. Public records and privacy TPF may publish transaction references, environmental verification and optional contributor attribution. An authenticated Pi username is not automatically published together with a wallet address. Public blockchain information remains independently accessible. See the Privacy Policy . Availability and changes TPF services may change and may depend on external platforms and environmental providers. Continuous availability is not guaranteed. These Terms may be updated; material changes will be communicated where required. Nothing here limits liability or rights that cannot legally be excluded.
transparency: The Pioneer Forest is a community-driven reforestation initiative operating within the Pi Network ecosystem. It is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Pi Core Team. TPF records contributions and planting, shares the proof, and keeps the history available. How Impact Is Created Pi contributions help fund tree planting through independent providers such as Tree-Nation. TPF chooses planting based on available projects, species, costs and the purpose of each contribution or pool. Tree-Nation supplies planting records and estimates of expected CO₂ capture. Those estimates describe capture over time; they do not mean that all the CO₂ has already been removed. Public Rules & Figures The current general minimum is 20 kg of estimated CO₂ capture per Pi contributed . Partner Pools are agreed individually through an offer; this minimum does not automatically apply to them. Products show their backing in the product details. See the reviewed planting and CO₂ totals → The website uses one published TPF summary, with a date showing how far the records have been checked. Tree-Nation’s current CO₂ calculations cover up to ten years of growth. Actual capture happens gradually and depends on the trees and site conditions. TPF uses “CO₂ capture” for these estimates and “CO₂ backing” for the values assigned to pools and products. A reward record is not automatically a formal carbon credit. Tree-Nation’s CO₂ methodology → Documentation & Public Record The Pioneer Forest maintains a public record of activity through multiple channels: The Impact page on this site Updates on the Fireside #ThePioneerForest channel External planting certificates where available Public blockchain transaction records These records let you follow a contribution and check the planting behind it. A planting certificate documents the planting and its stated CO₂ estimate; it does not by itself prove that capture is complete. Funding Model The Pioneer Forest operates primarily through voluntary Pi contributions. Contributions are not investments and do not grant ownership, financial returns, or decision-making rights. Funds support planting and the work needed to keep TPF running. What The Pioneer Forest Does Not Provide No ownership of trees or land No investment or financial product No guaranteed returns No legal claim over planted sites Independence TPF coordinates funding and keeps the records. Planting providers plant and manage the forests and supply planting records. TPF manages its website, accounting and public updates. Verification Pi transactions can be verified through the Pi Block Explorer . External planting activity can be reviewed through the Tree-Nation profile . Contact The Pioneer Forest is operated by egal42. You can contact egal42 through Pi Chats or the Fireside forum. Replies may take a little time.
